content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP® Certification in Portland

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires a combination of formal education and project-management experience. Review PMI's specific hour and degree requirements for the PMP®—most candidates meet them through a bachelor's degree plus documented project-leadership experience. Verify your background before enrolling.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP® course. Attend sessions at times that fit your Portland schedule. Our active certified practitioners deliver real-world project scenarios and PMI's official curriculum—all online, from start to finish.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After finishing the course, create your PMI account and formally apply for the PMP® credential. Provide your education, experience, and contact-hour proof. Pay PMI's exam fee and await approval—typically within two weeks.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Pass the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-prep resources, practice tests, and review sessions to solidify your knowledge. Schedule your exam with Pearson VUE. Sit for the computer-based test at an authorized center and demonstrate your project-management expertise.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP® Credential
steps_items.text: Your PMP® lasts three years. Earn Professional Development Units (PDUs) through approved training, volunteering, or work experience to renew. Granite PM Academy and PMI offer ongoing learning opportunities to keep your skills current and your credential active.

fq_items.question: Do I need to travel to {city} for this training?
fq_items.answer: No. All of our PMP training is delivered live-virtual via video conference, so {city} professionals attend from wherever they work. No commuting or hotel required.

fq_items.question: What are the PMP eligibility requirements?
fq_items.answer: PMI requires either a four-year degree with 36 months of project leadership experience, or a high school diploma with 60 months of experience. All applicants need 35 contact hours of PM education — our course satisfies this requirement.

fq_items.question: How long does it take to get PMP certified in {city}?
fq_items.answer: After completing training, PMI typically approves applications within 5–10 business days. Once approved, you have one year to sit for the exam. Most students study 4–8 weeks after the course before scheduling their exam.

fq_items.question: What is your pass guarantee?
fq_items.answer: If you complete our course and do not pass the PMP exam within 90 days, we provide additional coaching sessions at no additional cost until you pass.

fq_items.question: Is this training PMI-approved?
fq_items.answer: Yes. Granite PM Academy is a PMI Premier Authorized Training Partner (ATP). Our curriculum is aligned to PMI’s current Examination Content Outline and our contact hours are fully accepted by PMI.

Healthcare systems rely on certified professionals to oversee clinical IT, facility upgrades, and operational transformations. While not always mandatory, certification signals structured oversight capability and makes candidates more competitive in local hiring for advancement into formal PM positions.

fq_items.answer: Healthcare, financial services, and insurance employers in Portland's market most actively seek certified project managers. Certified professionals (PMP or CAPM holders) often command higher salaries and access to more senior opportunities within these sectors compared to non-certified peers.
